approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs using its retained crossover, mutation, sulfur-admission and survivor rules. At each batch it fits a raw-score count-fingerprint Gaussian process and conditions a fixed native tabular quantile model on the same accepted session records. The GP supplies both candidate location and the dependence of a joint Gaussian draw. Each standardized draw is transported through the native constant-tail quantile curve, centered on the GP location. The existing stall rule limits eligibility by GP mean, and sequential sampled maxima select the paid molecules. This Parent has already improved on the native-location recipe, while remaining below the formal Anchor.
approach.novelty: Replace the candidate-specific residual standard deviation by the standard deviation of the actual jittered GP factor, retaining the standardized native quantile shape, constant tails, GP location and original copula uniforms. This isolates the source of marginal amplitude on the translated native host. No completed same-Parent sibling is listed. The concurrently planned shape projection changes shape at native variance, and the coordinate adapter changes feature visibility; neither is combined here. Wider native intervals and better native pinball scores make useful search gain, rather than narrower intervals alone, the test.

observed_bottleneck: On code Parent n-e2506e11f536 all 435 native/GP allocation batches execute and 2608 active-only purchases versus native-location replay reach real feedback. Full positive score-minus-best-actual-generating-parent gain is 14.212983699997896, +3.023919577374297 versus n-16b934239c55, but late gain is 4.445967758637079 versus 4.943625601057764. Same-paid central-90% native-residual width is 0.17782235585517736 versus original GP 0.09878172042737944, and late width 0.2163807090041268 versus 0.11924409579804496. The contrary evidence is retained: native-residual pinball 0.02023840351299787 is better than GP 0.022170072530832197. Dispersion differs; harmful over-exploration is unproved. Parent mean 0.5589888753493724 (seed population SD 0.02055446360783425) is +0.08521606228482898 versus its native-location Parent but -0.04804144086175869 versus formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de. This supports the frozen amplitude-source test, not a calibration claim or separate credit to native uncertainty. Evidence: policy/nodes/n-e2506e11f536.json; policy/scratch/r0063-03-improve-L01/analyze/aggregate.json and its fifteen audit-seed-N-TASK.json files, each independently checked against its archived Search logs/trajectories by policy/scratch/r0064-02-improve-L01/plan/evidence-audit.json and the fifteen corresponding owned per-cell audits.

hypothesis: For candidate i retain its actual native constant-tail piecewise-linear Q_i and exact integrated m_i, with centered integrated variance v_i. Keep the original conditional GP mean mu_i, actual jittered pool factor F, original normal block N, d_i=sqrt(sum_j F_ij^2), z=(N@F.T)/d and u=Phi(z). For v_i>0 route S_i=mu_i+sigma_GP_i*(Q_i(u_i)-m_i)/sqrt(v_i), where sigma_GP_i=score_scale*d_i. This replaces only the candidate-wise amplitude source: the standardized native curve, tails and Gaussian-copula uniforms are preserved; the GP mean remains the exact mask and location consumer. A mathematically constant native row has zero variance and retains zero residual, explicitly unexposed to the amplitude replacement. Negative/nonfinite variance is numerical failure, never clamped. No multiplier, mixture, clipping, noise, kernel, schedule, checkpoint or feature adaptation is introduced.

finding_summary.headline: GP-scale transport increases generating-parent gain, while final score stays nearly unchanged
finding_summary.insights:
Candidate-wise scale matters for allocation even when location, eligibility, standardized shape and latent dependence are held fixed on each state. This is not uniform narrowing: the GP/native SD ratio spans 0.105 to 189.753 across pool rows, with median 0.964, while the purchased-row median is 1.057. The result rules out an entirely unexposed scale change and shows that the extra generating-parent gain survived real feedback and breeding. It does not establish reliable endpoint improvement, beneficial native uncertainty, or isolated contributions of the retained shape, copula and model. A child can beat its own generating parents without exceeding an already better incumbent; the full incumbent gain sums are nearly identical, 5.263227 versus 5.257451. The two borrowed principles—quantile integration and copula transport—operated, but constant tails and the GP-location/GP-scale/native-shape hybrid are campaign deviations, so the source literature supplies no performance guarantee.

The trajectories still show a method-level limitation beyond scale: late positive gains occur in only 240 of 2,175 purchases, while the leading molecular cohorts contain only 5–15 typed scaffolds despite 1,654 distinct typed scaffolds across the full output. The molecular assessment finds continued local substitutions and ring-size variants around a few productive families, together with chemically questionable attachments and missing stereochemical/charge alternatives. Very large molecules fell from 384 to 51, but tiny molecules rose from 23 to 166; late counts changed from 189 to 8 and from 12 to 68 respectively. Thus the output traded one size excursion for another without reliably preserving useful connected molecular context. This supports examining a context-preserving graph proposal operator or a search scheme that maintains several productive core families; their benefit remains untested. The evidence does not show universal scaffold collapse or prove that more diversity alone would improve scores. This node settles the registered finite-panel scale/gain prediction and leaves reliable endpoint gain, proposal quality and residual-shape usefulness open; it does not decide the fate of the approach.
finding_summary.results: The transport executed correctly in all 435 batches and all 69,600 candidate rows, with no constant-variance exceptions, numerical failures or fallbacks. It retained GP means, eligibility and copula inputs while matching GP marginal variance and native standardized shape. Every batch changed its purchased set relative to the old native-amplitude law on the same state: 2,947 of 4,350 positions changed and 2,323 paid identities were absent from that passive selection set. All 4,200 nonfinal purchases reached both models at the next fit, including 2,250 of those active-only identities. Summed positive gain over actual generating parents rose from the frozen 14.212984 baseline to 15.255768, a gain of 1.042784; 9 of 15 task/seed cells improved. This confirms the registered finite-panel useful-amplitude prediction. Late gain rose from 4.445968 to 5.021269 even though its positive-margin count fell from 259 to 240. The full count rose from 673 to 686. Mean final Top-1 was 0.559374 versus the code Parent’s 0.558989, only +0.000385, with two seed macros lower and one higher; 8 of 15 endpoints improved. Seed dispersion increased from 0.020554 to 0.031104. The mean remains 0.047656 below the formal Anchor, so the separate +0.002 criterion is unmet; task-safety margins and a protocol decision were not supplied. On identical purchased labels the active 90% interval narrowed from 0.124030 to 0.097432, but pinball loss worsened from 0.017926 to 0.018437 and 90% coverage fell from 0.681609 to 0.667816. These conditional diagnostics do not explain the useful-gain increase as better calibration.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides, dense heterocycles and neutral amines; tiny fragments, reactive attachments and undefined stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character: This assessment describes n-c303c83ca3e4 against the published code Parent n-e2506e11f536. All supplied trajectories were read: Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, all five tasks, 300 accepted records per cell including 10 initial records; the chemistry counts below use the 4350 optimizer records per node, counting recurrence across sessions. context.comparison separately establishes complete Child evaluation and complete matched Parent pairing, with no profile-mismatched seeds. No supplied task lacks trajectories and no listed input path is missing. Child evidence remains in the explicitly trusted .worktrees/slot-2/runs/staging/seed-{0,1,2}/trajectories paths outside runs/SPIRAL2; these are frozen-request citation authorities, not published Child archive files. Parent evidence is the published nodes/n-e2506e11f536/seed-{0,1,2}/trajectories files. No substitute archive path or unobserved comparison is asserted. The molecules are overwhelmingly connected ring-containing structures: RDKit perceives rings in 4159 and aromatic atoms in 4096 optimizer records. All 4350 are single connected components; the small-fragment issue below means small whole molecules, not dotted mixtures. The median is 30 heavy atoms, with a range of 1 to 119. The Parent also has median 30, but its mean is 35.1225 versus 29.3667 in the Child. Very large structures, at least 60 heavy atoms, fall from 384 Parent records to 51 Child records, while at-most-six-heavy-atom structures rise from 23 to 166. The corresponding late counts, optimizer ordinals 146 through 290, are 189 to 8 and 12 to 68 among 2175 records per node. Thus reduced giant-molecule growth accompanies more tiny-molecule proposals; neither tail alone characterizes the output. Distinct typed/generic Murcko scaffolds number 1654/1021 versus 1951/1305 in the Parent, including the empty scaffold. Within the separate 30-highest-score task cohorts, the Child retains 5 to 15 typed scaffolds; its high-score chemistry is clustered but not globally collapsed. Fragment-excluded within-cell top-30 Morgan-bit pairwise median similarities range from 0.3875 to 0.6237, a descriptive measure with no universal diversity threshold. The favorable chemistry includes recognizable indole carboxamides, amino-substituted aryl systems, tertiary amines and cyclic carbonyl compounds. However, 534 molecules bear N-halogen bonds, 63 bear O-halogen bonds, 149 bear O-O bonds, 155 bear carbon allenes, and 66 bear acyl halides. These are local structural flags, not measured instability or universal exclusions. The Parent counts are respectively 704, 161, 71, 119 and 29: liabilities shift rather than disappear. None has a formal charge or an assigned perceived tetrahedral center; 2270 Child and 2574 Parent records have an unassigned perceived center. Neutral SMILES do not establish absence of ionizable amines. Synthetic plausibility is a structure-based judgment; no route, isolation, stability, protonation or stereochemical experiment was supplied. The frozen digest string counters support the ring/aromatic reading and report zero charge/stereocenter markers on every task. Graph counts and score-linked examples are reproducible in policy/scratch/r0064-02-improve-L01/audit-seed-<N>-<task>.json; the separate molecular/trajectory-audit.json and validation receipt list exact inputs and hashes. The scope is accepted Search output, not every unpurchased candidate, an alternative adaptive history, or a component effect. Mask-conditioned chemistry and formal Anchor chemistry are not assessed here. Score associations do not establish mechanism activation, rank, selection, route feasibility or a missing target pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 accepted optimizer molecules have median 25 heavy atoms, range 2-45, and median three perceived rings. The digest ring/aromatic-bearing string rates are 0.9713/0.9644. The leading seed-2 family is a mostly planar indole-2-carboxamide attached to an aniline phenyl ring, with methoxy, methyl and nitrile substitutions. Seed 2 evaluation 250 has 25 heavy atoms and three rings, an N-phenyl-N-(mercaptomethyl) amide, and score 0.5278825388902705; evaluation 215 is the simpler N-methyl anilide at 0.5188745216627708. These are recognizable medicinal-chemistry frameworks, although the thiol-bearing arm introduces a distinct reactivity concern. Seed 0 instead ends near N-fluoro hydrazide/indole analogues, with its best at evaluation 298, 0.4163503402962837. Seed 1 favors a phenol-substituted partially saturated diazacycle with an N-fluoro arylamino substituent, best evaluation 291, 0.4478476056206344. Thus the pooled highest examples should not be mistaken for uniform convergence across seeds. The Parent also produced indole amides and nitrogen heterocycles, but its nitrile-bearing optimizer records number only 5 versus 213 here; this is a chemical-coverage association, not attribution to the changed algorithm component.
liabilities: N-halogen attachments occur in 169 optimizer records, including the highest examples from seeds 0 and 1. Those are chemically different from ordinary carbon-bound aryl fluorides.
The best seed-2 example contains a free thiol arm; the final cohort includes an O-O-S linkage at evaluation 296. Neither high score nor graph validity establishes storage or synthetic stability.
There are 25 whole molecules with at most six heavy atoms, alongside otherwise substantial aromatic scaffolds.
missing_features: The high-scoring compact nitrile/aromatic-amide arrangement is not retained across every seed or every late proposal; some late edits lose its nitrile or aromatic connectivity. This is incomplete access and preservation, not global absence of those groups.

There is no evidence here for a particular unseen required pharmacophore. Explicit stereochemical and ionization alternatives are absent from the output, but these trajectories do not establish that either would improve this objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy fluoroanilide at evaluation 9 scores 0.3051048083696145. In the high seed-2 family, retaining the aromatic indole/anilide core together with a nitrile accompanies scores around 0.50; 29 of the pooled top 30 have a nitrile and all retain an amide. Seed 2 evaluation 299, with an ethynyl substituent and no nitrile, scores 0.41001491492622644; evaluation 300, with the indole region enlarged and partly dearomatized, scores 0.3360595432279983. These multi-edit comparisons support the intact compact aromatic-carbonyl arrangement, without isolating one substituent effect. Tiny FNOF and FNS molecules score 0.0. The Parent best values by seeds 0/1/2 are 0.44989726212142783, 0.4454539912731944 and 0.43554057891621306; the Child chemistry changes are not a uniform favorable shift across seeds.

per_task.generated_character: The accepted stream has median 35 heavy atoms, range 1-98, and median six perceived rings; digest ring/aromatic-bearing rates are 0.931/0.9264. It contains several chemically distinct families. The seed-1 best at evaluation 288, 0.6263976665046184, is a 36-heavy-atom, seven-ring polyaza aromatic assembly with methoxy, nitrile, O-C#N and butyl substituents; RDKit perceives a four-membered ring among its extensively fused rings. The O-C#N attachment is an organic cyanate, distinct from the carbon-bound nitrile elsewhere in the same molecule. Seed 0 evaluation 261, 0.6209396568099791, has 45 heavy atoms and nine rings, multiple cyclic carbonyls, an N-ethoxycarbonyl group, compact fused O heterocycles and an O-CH2-S-Cl substituent. Seed 2 reaches 0.6196842373312962 at evaluation 292 with a more conventional three-ring linked azaaryl framework carrying amino, dialkylamino, chloro and fluoromethyl substituents. The Parent median is 42.5 heavy atoms and 346 records have at least 60; here those large records number 27. Smaller size does not by itself make the highly fused Child structures straightforward synthetic targets.
liabilities: Four-membered fused rings occur in conspicuous high-score examples; 22 of the pooled top 30 bear a three- or four-membered perceived ring. This requires structural scrutiny rather than a route-level verdict.
Organic cyanates, sulfur-halogen attachments and occasional acyl halides appear alongside familiar azaaromatics and ethers; the score does not certify their stability.
Although extreme growth is much reduced against the Parent, both 54 tiny and 27 at-least-60-heavy-atom records remain. The top-30 cohort in each seed contains four typed Murcko scaffolds.
missing_features: Meaningful substituted heteroaromatic connectivity is absent in the 54 at-most-six-heavy-atom proposals, despite its presence in the higher-scoring families.

The trajectories do not identify a missing target decoration or mandatory larger scaffold. They show incomplete coverage of similarly decorated cores with ordinary ring sizes and attachment chemistry; whether such alternatives improve the score is unmeasured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial cyclic dicarbonyl heteroaromatic ester scores 0.548381482770623; the subsequent linked/fused heteroaromatic families reach roughly 0.62. In contrast, FF at seed 1 evaluation 292 and small alkane/thioether examples lie at the observed 0.5 floor. The gradient therefore distinguishes substantial substituted heteroaromatic arrangements from tiny molecules, while giving little information among the chemically disparate floor examples. An elaborate seven-ring system and the seed-2 linked three-ring aminoheteroaryl system both approach the leading scores, so these observations do not imply that increasing ring count or molecular size is intrinsically rewarded. The Parent best values by seeds 0/1/2 are 0.60808124728244, 0.6284615865474776 and 0.5982257793697878. Its seed-1 best already uses a substantially smaller fused heteroaromatic architecture than its very large tail.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer records have median 33 heavy atoms, range 1-119, and median three rings; the digest ring/aromatic-bearing rates are 0.954/0.9483 and halogen-bearing rate is 0.9805. The high-scoring molecules combine two aromatic rings with exposed neutral amines, alkyl linkers and chlorine/fluorine substitution. Seed 1 evaluation 298, 0.9687606422301431, is a 32-heavy-atom diaryl/benzyl structure with a flexible butyl-methyl tertiary amine side chain, methoxy, aniline and chloroalkyl groups. Seed 2 evaluation 286, 0.9675150634036055, has 33 heavy atoms and three rings: a substituted aminophenol/anisole ring joined through a ketone-containing chain to an N-methyl aminopyrrolidine bearing a dichlorophenyl group. Related piperidine and unsaturated-linker variants remain high. Seed 0 takes a different course: its best, evaluation 293 at 0.9243692205010495, is a larger fused/bridged aryl-amine arrangement containing a cyclic allene. The Parent favors more ring-dense systems, median five rings at the same median heavy-atom count; its seed-1 best is a compact multiring amine cage at 0.994627130457666. Thus both flexible and rigid amine architectures are represented.
liabilities: There are 140 carbon-allene-bearing records, including the seed-0 best with an allene embedded in a ring; aromatic content and a high score do not resolve geometry or strain.
There are 89 O-O-bearing records, including five of the pooled top 30. Late examples also carry O-Cl or O-S bonds. These local motifs complicate a simple drug-like interpretation.

Extensively halogenated aromatic systems and flexible tertiary-amine chains can raise physicochemical questions, but no lipophilicity, solubility, assay selectivity or measured liability is supplied. The 34 tiny and 21 very large proposals show size excursions too.
missing_features: Appropriately exposed neutral amines linked to substantial aryl frameworks are abundant among the high-scoring examples but absent from several low sulfonyl fragments and late truncated products. Basic amines are not a generator-wide missing feature.

All pooled top-30 examples have an unassigned perceived tetrahedral center. Defined configurations and explicit protonation alternatives are absent; these scores do not reveal which configuration or charge state, if any, is preferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: All pooled top-30 Child molecules contain the audit-defined free aliphatic amine motif and two aromatic rings; none contains a sulfonyl group. The low seed-0 evaluation-20 sulfonamide-bearing pyrrolidine ketone scores 0.00021169315013374197, and evaluation 12, a small dichlorophenyl sulfonate ester, scores 0.00024675866379847753. This is consistent with favorable exposed-amine/aryl geometry in the observed series, not with halogen substitution alone. However, it is not a causal sulfur penalty: size, connectivity and amine availability also change, and the Parent high-score seed-0 molecule retains a sulfonamide. The very small late seed-2 aminophenol/O-S fragment at evaluation 295 scores 0.012240058946324248 while the intact framework at evaluation 300 scores 0.9648611637321857. The Parent seed-2 best, 0.8420875941513817, is much more cage-like than the Child seed-2 amine/ketone series; this is an observed family contrast rather than evidence about a docking pose or binding interaction.

per_task.generated_character: The output has median 32 heavy atoms, range 1-66, and median five rings, with digest ring/aromatic-bearing rates 0.969/0.9609. The seed-2 leading series combines an ethoxy-substituted naphthalene-like aromatic region with fused or bridged partly saturated nitrogen rings and cyclic amide carbonyls. The best at evaluation 271, 0.2355923605152486, has 31 heavy atoms and five perceived rings, including a four-membered ring. Its analogues change N-alkyl groups, ring size and small side chains while retaining the cyclic dicarbonyl arrangement. Seed 0 evaluation 268, 0.2229773722655237, and seed 1 evaluation 279, 0.22397030352974137, use less fused aryl-substituted diaza/lactam frameworks with medium-to-large rings. These structures contain familiar individual amide, ether and aryl motifs, but their assembled ring topology and undefined configurations make synthetic plausibility uncertain. The Parent also generates cyclic carbonyl/nitrogen systems: median heavy atoms remains 32, but median aromatic rings falls from three in the Parent to two in the Child. There are 78 Child records with a perceived ring of at least nine atoms versus 339 in the Parent; the Child samples more compact fused arrangements.
liabilities: All pooled top-30 examples contain a perceived three- or four-membered ring; favorable graph-level scores do not establish strain tolerance or a practical construction route.
Complex N-N/N-O-containing variants and crowded ring junctions occur. No proposed structure resolves tetrahedral stereochemistry.

The full stream includes 27 tiny whole molecules and two at least 60-heavy-atom structures. Distinct typed scaffolds number 527, so local concentration should not be called complete structural collapse.
missing_features: Defined stereoisomers are absent even though all pooled top-30 Child molecules have unassigned perceived centers and small rings. Their configuration-dependent behavior is not measured.

The record shows many local fused-ring variants but does not demonstrate multiple substantially different, similarly productive placements of the aromatic and cyclic-carbonyl regions within each seed. No specific missing reference pharmacophore can be inferred from these trajectories.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial N-methyl cyclic dicarbonyl aromatic ester scores 0.1678386594791329. The late aryl/cyclic-carbonyl systems reach about 0.22-0.236, whereas C, C=C, C#C and other tiny examples have score 0.0. All pooled top-30 Child molecules preserve an amide motif and two aromatic rings. Within the leading seed-2 scaffold, evaluation 265 scores 0.23406293322712937, evaluation 271 scores 0.2355923605152486 and the larger altered final evaluation 300 scores 0.23056651868870703: extra ring complexity is not accompanied by monotonic improvement. The Parent seed-0 best reaches 0.2363146341487732 with a different, less tightly fused aryl/cyclic-carbonyl architecture. These observations favor maintaining the combined aryl and carbonyl/nitrogen arrangement over fragmentation, without identifying a unique topology or an unseen required motif.

per_task.generated_character: The accepted stream has median 26 heavy atoms, range 1-62, and median three rings, with ring/aromatic-bearing digest rates 0.9552/0.908. The best chemistry is not uniformly aromatic: seed 2 evaluation 287, 0.6653453857050924, is a 26-heavy-atom, two-ring, partly saturated fused azaheterocycle bearing a carbonyl, exocyclic imine, two N-F bonds, a fluorinated alkenyl side chain and a fluoroethyl ester. Its perceived ring sizes are four and six. An aromatic fused analogue at seed 2 evaluation 143 scores 0.5596216551471145, and larger-ring analogues also occur. Seed 0 evaluation 253, 0.4865308584507047, is a three-ring fluorinated heterocycle with urea/formyl chemistry; seed 1 evaluation 282, 0.4364450888763128, is a six-ring nitrogen/oxygen-rich framework with a small-ring substituent, N-S bond and acyl fluoride. The Parent likewise uses fluorinated heterocycles and small-ring architectures, but its median size/ring count is 28 heavy atoms/five rings versus 26/three here. These are chemically diverse fluorinated cyclic carbonyl/imine systems with substantial local-bonding liabilities, not a demonstrated conventional medicinal series.
liabilities: Two N-F bonds are present in the best example and N-halogen bonds occur in 292 optimizer records. Valence-valid N-fluorination is distinct from ordinary C-F decoration and cannot be assumed chemically interchangeable.

Small fused rings, exocyclic imines, conjugated unsaturated esters, N-S bonds and acyl fluorides occur across the seed-best families. Individual motifs can be real chemistry, but stability and a practical route are untested.
There are 500 records with an unassigned perceived tetrahedral center, 26 tiny whole molecules and one at least 60-heavy-atom structure.
missing_features: Late truncated heterocycles lack the substantial linker/ester arrangement carried by the best observed family. Reliable retention of that arrangement is incomplete even within the productive seed.

Comparable high-scoring alternatives with ordinary carbon-bound fluorine and without N-F attachments are poorly represented in the pooled leading cohort: 28 of the top 30 contain N-halogen bonds. These observations do not establish that replacing N-F would improve the score.

Explicit stereochemical alternatives are absent, including for the partially saturated fused best molecule; the record cannot identify a preferred configuration or a missing target-specific amine motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: A very large, linked heterocyclic ester/amide combination at seed 1 evaluation 15 scores 3.2416258040348776e-69, while O at evaluation 67 scores 3.3466049979681925e-24. Neither indiscriminate growth nor reduction to a tiny molecule is favorable in this record. The initial cyclic dicarbonyl ester scores 0.0020944534688323298. In seed 2, keeping the extended ester/unsaturated-chain arrangement together with the fluorinated heterocycle accompanies much higher scores: evaluation 104 scores 0.5562692819086457 and evaluation 143 scores 0.5596216551471145. The partly saturated fused variant at evaluation 287 is higher still. Conversely, late isolated N-fluorinated cores at evaluations 296 and 297 score 5.1432402107593555e-09 and 2.780754963288755e-09. The final methyl-ketone variant at evaluation 300 scores 0.3364594222694713, below the ester-containing best. The visible gradient supports the whole arrangement of size, carbonyl/ester, linker and fluorinated nitrogen-rich core, not fluorination alone. The Parent seed-best values 0.506913769157628, 0.6467462742507727 and 0.6166736435591553 come from different fluorinated ring families; the Child does not consistently cover similarly high regions across seeds.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: n-c303c83ca3e4, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, batch ten and 290 accepted optimizer records per session; paired published n-e2506e11f536 under the same panel. Among 4350 Child records, 534 bear N-halogen, 63 O-halogen, 149 O-O, 155 carbon-allene and 66 acyl-halide motifs; Parent counts are 704, 161, 71, 119 and 29. High-score examples themselves include N-F, O-O, O-S and cyclic-allene motifs. Familiar neutral amines, amides, aryl ethers and carbon-bound halogens are also present, so the limitation is inconsistent local chemistry rather than total inability to generate ordinary bonds.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve ordinary local bonding while elaborating otherwise substantial ring and linker systems.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A general generator would need access to chemically familiar attachment alternatives while retaining useful core and linker arrangements, and distinguish attachment-atom identity from whole-scaffold identity. Treat the observed motifs as explicit structural hypotheses, not a task answer or a universal blacklist; current-session labels must determine search value. This association does not attribute the problem to the changed component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: n-c303c83ca3e4 on Search seeds 0/1/2 with batch ten and 290 accepted optimizer records per session, compared with published n-e2506e11f536 on the same panel. All 4350 Child optimizer records lack assigned perceived tetrahedral centers and formal charges, while 2270 contain at least one unassigned perceived center; the Parent has 2574 such records and likewise no assigned centers or formal charge. Exposed tertiary amines, small fused rings and substituted cyclic carbonyl systems occur among high-score examples. Neutral strings do not establish nonionizability, and no configuration-specific or protonation-specific benefit was observed.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output omits explicit configuration and ionization alternatives for many stereogenic, potentially ionizable molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic representation and edit capability would need to express chemically meaningful stereoisomers and charge states where applicable, preserving canonical identity and using only current-session observations. This is a demonstrated coverage gap, not evidence that adding a charge or selecting an arbitrary configuration will raise scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: n-c303c83ca3e4, complete Search seeds 0/1/2, batch ten and 290 optimizer records per session, with paired published n-e2506e11f536. At-most-six-heavy-atom records rise from 23 to 166 while at-least-60-heavy-atom records fall from 384 to 51; the corresponding late counts among 2175 records per node are 12 to 68 and 189 to 8. High-score examples commonly retain substantial combined ring/linker/functional-group arrangements, whereas late isolated cores and tiny whole molecules can have very low observed scores. Every accepted molecule is a single connected component, so this concerns size and loss of molecular context, not disconnected SMILES components.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful scaffold elaboration is not reliably retained across both collapse to tiny molecules and excessive whole-molecule growth.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: General graph edits would need to retain meaningful connected molecular context while exploring alternative ring and linker arrangements at multiple sizes. Keep both tails and late behavior observable; neither a universal lower bound nor a universal size cap follows from these data. The tradeoff is descriptive for this source and panel, not an attributed effect or a route-level judgment.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: n-c303c83ca3e4, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, batch ten and 290 optimizer records per session. The full stream contains 1654 typed and 1021 generic Murcko scaffolds, including the empty scaffold, but separate pooled 30-highest-score task cohorts contain only 5 to 15 typed scaffolds. Their chemistry often consists of local substitutions or ring-size changes around one family. The three sessions of one heteroaromatic series each have four typed scaffolds in their own highest-score 30. Fragment-excluded within-cell top-30 median pairwise Morgan similarities span 0.3875 to 0.6237; there is clustering but no universal collapse. The paired Parent has 1951 typed and 1305 generic scaffolds overall, which does not establish that more scaffolds would be better.
transferable_gaps.gap: Many distinct accepted graphs do not consistently provide several chemically different productive core families within each session.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Retain access to substantive changes in core connectivity and ring geometry as well as peripheral analogues, and distinguish chemical-family coverage from string novelty. Preserve already observed useful group arrangements without encoding benchmark identities or reference structures. Any diversity intervention remains a conditional hypothesis whose usefulness must be learned from current-session feedback; the chemistry comparison is not component attribution.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
